summary: Most visitors — including EU, UK, US and Indian passport holders — need Azerbaijan's ASAN e-Visa, issued online in about three working days for a 30-day stay. CIS neighbors, Turkey, the Gulf states, China, Japan and South Korea enter visa-free, and citizens of Armenia are barred from entry.

notes: The UK and Canadian governments' travel advice says you need an export certificate to take antiques or art — such as carpets, samovars, copperware or paintings — out of Azerbaijan; the vendor or the Azerbaijan National Carpet Museum can provide one.

Canada's travel advice says some prescription medicines may not be available and that you are responsible for checking whether yours are legal in Azerbaijan; keep them in the original container with a copy of the prescription.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says that outside major businesses credit cards may not always be accepted, and that several ATMs in major cities dispense both US dollars and Azerbaijani manat.

safety.text: The UK government's travel advice says crime levels in Baku are generally low. It advises against all travel within 5 km of the closed border with Armenia (Nakhchivan excepted) and against all but essential travel to some areas in south-western Azerbaijan, in and around the former Nagorno-Karabakh region, because of mines and unexploded weapons; entering certain areas there without the authorities' permission is illegal.

tips.text: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the Azerbaijani authorities' permission could be denied entry, and advises contacting an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate before you travel. The border with Armenia is closed.

Canada's travel advice says all land border crossings have been closed to passengers since 2020, except for freight, so visitors can only enter by air. The UK government says entry by land or sea is restricted and that you need the authorities' permission to leave by road.

The UK government's travel advice says that if you stay longer than 15 days you must register with the State Migration Service, online or in person, and that if you do not you will have to pay a fine before you can leave. Hotels often do this for their guests; otherwise you must do it yourself.
Apply for the e-Visa on the official ASAN Visa portal, evisa.gov.az.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Most travelers do, but it's easy. Citizens of many countries, including the EU, UK, US and India, apply online for the ASAN e-Visa (USD 29, about three working days, 30-day stay). CIS countries, Georgia, Turkey, the Gulf states, China, Japan and South Korea are visa-free, and the remaining nationalities apply at an embassy.

faq.question: How fast is the ASAN e-Visa?
faq.answer: Standard processing takes about three working days. An urgent service issues the e-Visa within roughly three hours for a higher fee. The visa is valid for 90 days from issue for a single 30-day stay.

faq.question: Can I enter Azerbaijan if I have been to Armenia?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the Azerbaijani authorities' permission could be denied entry, and advises contacting an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate before you travel. No official source we could read says how a visit to Armenia itself is treated at the border.

faq.question: Can I cross into Azerbaijan by land?
faq.answer: Generally no. Canada's travel advice says all land border crossings have been closed since 2020 except for freight, so visitors can only enter by air. The UK government says the land borders with Georgia and Iran are temporarily closed, though British nationals may be able to cross from Iran at Astara with special authorisation arranged through the British Embassy in Baku.

faq.question: Do I need to register my stay in Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Yes, if you stay more than 15 days. The UK government's travel advice says you must register with the State Migration Service, online or in person, and that if you do not you will have to pay a fine before you can leave. Hotels often register their guests; otherwise you must do it yourself.
